title: The Portuguese Gambit
description: This repertoire features both the Portuguese and Icelandic Gambits and is a great attacking weapon for Black.

2kr1b1r/ppp1pppp/2n5/3q4/6b1/3P1N2/PPP1B.text:
White opens up the dark-squared bishop.

We'll occupy the center with e5. Our central control is better than White's.

2kr1b1r/ppp2ppp/2n5/3qp3/6b1/3PBN2/PPP1B.text:
White develops the bishop.

Let's further strengthen our center.

2kr1b1r/ppp3pp/2n2p2/3qpb2/8/3PBN1P/PPP1.text: After ...Bf5, Black has better control over the center, and is ready for a kingside pawn-storm.

r1b1kb1r/ppp1pppp/2n5/3q4/3P4/4B3/PPP2PP.text:
White supports d4 with the bishop.

Against 6.c3, ...e5 is a good move to make use of White's passivity.

We'll continue developing our queenside.

r1bq1rk1/pp2ppbp/2n3p1/2p5/2BP4/2P1BN2/P.text:
And with ...Nc6 we add further pressure to the d4-pawn. 

We can even jump to a5 to hunt the light-squared bishop.

r1bqkb1r/pp2pppp/1nn5/2p5/8/1BNP1N2/PPP2.text:
White brings out the knight to f3.

And we continue to develop our queenside.

r2qkb1r/pp3ppp/1nn1p3/2p2b2/8/1BNP1N2/PP.text:
After ...e6, ...Be7 with O-O follows with a very comfortable position.

We'll have a plan to improve the knight with ...Nd4 and add control to the c-file with ...Rc8.

r3kb1r/ppp1pppp/2n5/3q1b2/2PP4/4B3/PP3PP.text: White expands with c4 and attacks our queen.

r3kb1r/ppp1pppp/2n5/3q4/6b1/5N2/PPPPBPPP.text: White gets their king into safety, and so do we.

r3kb1r/ppp1pppp/2n5/5b2/2PPq3/4B3/PP3PPP.text:
The queen controls the light-squares and cannot be easily pushed away from e4. 

We'll castle queenside to add pressure to the d4-pawn.

rn2kb1r/ppp1pppp/8/3q4/6b1/5N2/PPPPBPPP/.text:
White breaks the pin and prepares to castle.

Let's continue developing.

rnb1kb1r/ppp1pppp/8/3q4/3P4/8/PPP2PPP/R1.text:
White occupies the center immediately, with d4.

Let's develop as well as pressuring the pawn.

rnb1kb1r/ppp1pppp/8/3q4/8/5N2/PPPP1PPP/R.text:
White starts to develop the kingside.

Our bishop has a nice square now.

rnbq1rk1/ppp1ppbp/6p1/8/2BP4/2P2N2/P1P2P.text:
White does as well.

We'll play c5 and challenge White's center.

rnbqkb1r/pp2pppp/1n6/2p5/8/1BNP4/PPP2PPP.text:
White stops our c4-plan.

We'll develop our other knight.

rnbqkb1r/ppp1pp1p/6p1/8/3P4/2P2N2/P1P2PP.text:
White pushes d4 to fight for the center.

We develop our king's bishop.

rnbqkb1r/ppp1pp1p/6p1/8/3P4/2P5/P1P2PPP/.text: And after ...g6 we transpose into the previous quoted line.

rnbqkb1r/ppp1pppp/1n6/8/8/1BN5/PPPP1PPP/.text:
White retreats to b3.

Black has a nice plan of gaining some space on the queenside.

rnbqkb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/3P4/8/2N5/PPPP1PPP.text:
At the club level, this is the most popular move with about 40% occurrence.

After ...Nxd5, Black's position often ends up being very promising.

rnbqkb1r/ppp1pppp/8/3N4/8/8/PPPP1PPP/R1B.text:
In nearly half of the games, White trades on d5, not allowing Black's strong knight to stay centralized.

Our queen recaptures.

rnbqkb1r/ppp1pppp/8/3n4/2B5/2N5/PPPP1PPP.text:
In about 15% of the games, White develops the bishop to c4 and adds an attacker to our knight.

We'll retreat the knight to b6, counterattacking the bishop.

rnbqkb1r/ppp1pppp/8/3n4/3P4/2N5/PPP2PPP/.text:
In 10% of games, White pushes d4 to immediately fight for the center.

We'll capture on c3.

rnbqkb1r/ppp1pppp/8/3n4/8/2N2N2/PPPP1PPP.text:
This move occurs in about 11% of the games in the database. White continues by developing the kingside knight.

We'll exchange knights.

rnbqkb1r/ppp1pppp/8/8/8/2P2N2/P1PP1PPP/R.text:
In 81% of the games, White recaptures with the b-pawn, not wanting to trade the queens.

We'll get ready to fianchetto.

rnbqkbnr/ppp1pppp/8/3P4/8/8/PPPP1PPP/RNB.text:
White usually captures the d5-pawn.

We won't recapture right away, but develop instead.

rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/RNB.text:
Welcome to The Portuguese Gambit Course! 

The Portuguese Gambit is a fighting opening that clearly follows basic opening principles and often allows for an active position with clear, easy-to-follow plans! 

It starts just like the Scandinavian, but we'll opt for development, instead of recapturing immediately on d5 with the queen. 

Let's check it out!

2kr1b1r/ppp1qppp/2n1bn2/8/2P5/2N2N2/PP1P.text:
Since White hasn't pushed d4, the weaknesses on d3/d4 and c2 are more apparent with our knight coming to b4. 

...g5 and ...g4, to gain some kingside space, is also an interesting plan to execute!

2kr3r/ppp2ppp/2n1bn2/3P4/1qP5/8/PP1Q1PPP.text:
But we can simply castle queenside and pin the d5-pawn to the queen. 

With ...Rhe8 coming, our advantage relies on the lead in development.

2krr3/ppp1bppp/2n2n2/5b2/2PP4/P3BN2/1P3P.text: And with ...Rhe8 we can plan to pressure the bishop on e3, with ...Ng4 coming.

r3k2r/ppp1bppp/2n2n2/5b2/2PP4/P4N2/1P3PP.text:
White defends the b4-square, as our knight was threatening to invade there.

Let's get our king into safety.

r3k2r/ppp2ppp/2n1bn2/3P4/1qP5/8/PP1Q1PPP.text: White advances with d5, thinking that they've forked our pieces.

r3kb1r/ppp1Qppp/2n2n2/5b2/2PP4/5N2/PP3PP.text:
White accepts our offer.

We continue to develop.

r3kb1r/ppp1qppp/2n1bn2/8/2PP4/5N2/PP2QPP.text:
White pushes in the center., threatening a fork with d5.

The most active approach is to offer a queen trade.

rn1qk2r/ppp2ppp/4b3/8/1bPPn3/2N5/PP1B1PP.text:
White blocks the pin in a quarter of the games.

But now the d4-pawn falls.

rn1qk2r/ppp2ppp/4b3/8/1bPPn3/2N5/PP2NPPP.text:
White supports c3 with Ne2.

This isn't that popular because they're blocking in the bishop, but it still happens and people forget about c4.

We'll take the pawn!

rn1qk2r/ppp2ppp/4bn2/8/1bPP4/2N5/PP3PPP/.text:
This move is played in 80% of the time this position is reached. White blocks the check with the knight. 

It isn't the strongest move, and allows for some counterplay.

We'll attack the pinned knight with Ne4.

rn1qk2r/ppp2ppp/4bn2/8/1bPP4/8/PP1B1PPP/.text:
Blocking with the bishop is an option. White doesn't mind trading on d2.

To keep active, we'll reinforce our bishop.

rn1qk2r/ppp2ppp/8/8/1bbPn3/P1N5/1P2NPPP/.text:
White attacks our bishop on b4.

Activity is the answer here. Black can ignore the bishop and threaten checkmate on f2.

rn1qkb1r/ppp2ppp/4bn2/8/2P5/2N5/PP1P1PPP.text:
In 15% of the games, White goes for the queenside knight development.

We can threaten a similar tactic to the previous line.

rn1qkb1r/ppp2ppp/4bn2/8/2P5/5N2/PP1P1PPP.text:
The second most popular move, occurring in 22% of games. 

White develops the knight to its natural square. Meanwhile, we can threaten a tactic by playing Qe7.

rn1qkb1r/ppp2ppp/4bn2/8/2PP4/8/PP3PPP/RN.text:
27% of players here have chosen 5.d4. White takes control over the center.

Let's continue our development with tempo, giving a check on b4.

rn2k2r/ppp1qppp/8/8/2bPn3/P1N3P1/1P3P1P/.text: But the queen slides back to e7, eyeing White's king. White has no time to take on c4, because we would have a lethal discovery with Nxc3+.

rn2k2r/ppp2ppp/4b3/8/1bP1q3/8/PP1B1PPP/R.text:
And we recapture on e4 with check. 

We can trade the bishops on d2 next, and continue to develop with ...Nc6 and ...O-O-O.

rn2k2r/ppp2ppp/4bn2/8/1qPP4/8/PP1Q1PPP/R.text: White offers a queen trade, but we'll reinforce on b4 yet again with a developing move.

rn2k2r/ppp2ppp/8/8/1bbPn2q/P1N3P1/1P2NP1.text:
White defends against it.

We cannot move both attacked pieces, so we'll have to trade on c3.

rn2k2r/ppp2ppp/8/8/2bPn2q/P1N3P1/1P3P1P/.text:
White recaptures with the knight.

Now we have three pieces en prise.

rn2kb1r/ppp1qppp/4bn2/8/2P5/2N5/PP1PQPPP.text:
White stops our plan.

We'll continue by developing our queenside.

rn2kb1r/ppp1qppp/4bn2/8/2P5/5N2/PP1PQPPP.text:
White prevents the threat of ...Bxc4+ with Qe2.

We continue to develop.

rnbqkb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/3P4/2P5/8/PP1P1PPP.text:
Close to 20% of the games, White pushes c4 and tries to hold on to the d5-pawn. 

This number represents more than 8 million games!

Now we'll play our gambit, with e6, sacrificing a pawn for speedy development.

rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/4Pn2/8/2P5/8/PP1P1PPP/R.text:
In 75% of the cases, White will go for the material gains and captures another pawn. 

Our bishop gets to an aggressive central location.

rnbqkbnr/ppp1pppp/8/3P4/8/8/PPPP1PPP/RNB.text:
More often than not White grabs on d5.

We bring our knight to f6.

rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/RNB.text:
Welcome to the second chapter! 

The Icelandic Gambit starts just like the Portuguese, but White protects their d5-pawn with c4. 

After that, Black offers yet another pawn in order to speed up their development!

Let's get into it!

r1b1kb1r/ppp1qppp/1nn5/8/8/1BN2N2/PP1PQP.text: White blocks the check with the queen.

r1bqk2r/ppp2ppp/1nnb4/8/8/1BN5/PP1PNPPP/.text: After ...Bd6, kingside castling will come with a comfortable position where all of our minor pieces are doing great.

r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/1nn5/8/8/1BN2N2/PP1P1PP.text:
White prepares to castle kingside, with a 50% occurrence.
 
We give a check on e7. This will either disrupt White's coordination or compel them to trade the queens into an endgame where we have the better pawn structure.

r1bqkb1r/ppp2ppp/1nn5/8/8/1BN5/PP1PNPPP/.text: White might opt for Nge2, developing this way instead.

r2q1rk1/ppp2ppp/2n2n2/8/1bBP2b1/2N1BN2/P.text: White protects it with the bishop.

r3kb1r/ppp1qppp/1nn5/8/6b1/1BN2N2/PP1PQP.text:
The bishop pins the knight on f3 and finally frees up the space for our king to castle. 

The queens will get exchanged, and our pawn structure is much better!

r4rk1/ppp2ppp/2nq1n2/8/1bBP2b1/2N1BN2/PP.text:
...Qd6 leaves room for the a-rook to join the attack on the isolated d4-pawn. 

We'll add further pressure to it by rerouting with ...Ba5 and ...Bb6.

rn1q1rk1/ppp2ppp/5n2/8/1bBP2b1/2N2N2/PP3.text:
White castles.

We'll develop our last minor piece, putting pressure on the d4-pawn.

rnbq1rk1/ppp2ppp/5n2/3p4/1bPP4/2N2N2/PP2.text:
Our opponent prepares to castle.

I recommend trading on c4 to disrupt White's coordination.

rnbq1rk1/ppp2ppp/5n2/8/1bBP4/2N2N2/PP3PP.text:
White recaptures, so they aren't left with any material losses.

Let's keep developing.

rnbqk2r/ppp2ppp/5n2/3p4/1bPP4/2N2N2/PP3P.text:
White gets out the other knight.

Let's get our king into safety.

rnbqkb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/3P4/2P5/8/PP1P1PPP.text:
White supports the d5-pawn with c4.

Black offers another pawn.

rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/1n6/8/8/1BN5/PP1P1PPP/R.text:
White saves the bishop.

We'll develop our other knight.

rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/3P4/2P5/2N5/PP1P1P.text:
In 12% of the games (representing close to 400,000 games) White doesn't accept our gambit and develops the knight instead.

White has already brought out a piece, so simply waiting for them to capture on e6 wouldn't give us any benefit.

rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/3P4/2PP4/8/PP3PPP/.text:
This move is in the minority. It occurs in about 5% of all games recorded in the online database. 

White occupies the center with the pawn. Trading on d5 allows us to free up the light-squared bishop.

rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/5n2/3P4/8/2N5/PP1P1PPP/.text:
White recaptures.

We don't have a good way of speeding up our development, so let's recapture.

rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/5n2/3p4/2PP4/2N5/PP3PPP.text:
White develops the knight to c3, adding some pressure to the d5-pawn.

Let's support it indirectly.

rnbqkb1r/ppp2ppp/8/3n4/2B5/2N5/PP1P1PPP/.text:
The bishop attacks our knight. 

Let's move it with tempo.

rnbqkbnr/ppp1pppp/8/3P4/8/8/PPPP1PPP/RNB.text:
White captures.

We'll bring our knight out.

rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/RNB.text:
The second study covers other fourth moves, where White doesn't capture on e6 — 4.Nc3 and 4.d4. 

Let's check them out!

2kr1b1r/ppp1pppp/2n2n2/3q4/3P1N2/2P5/PP3.text: White attacks our queen in return.

2kr1b1r/ppp1pppp/2n2n2/5q2/3P1N2/2P5/PP3.text:
f5 is a safe square for the queen. 

...e5 is coming!

2kr1b1r/ppp1pppp/2n2nq1/3P4/8/2N2QN1/PPP.text:
White unpins.

Now we have to save the knight. We'll fork the queen and the c2-pawn.

2kr1b1r/ppp1pppp/2n2nq1/8/3P4/4B1N1/PPP1.text:
White retreats the knight, intending to push c3 and support the d4-pawn.

Black should play actively in the center.

2kr1b1r/ppp1pppp/5nq1/3P4/3n4/2N1Q1N1/PP.text:
White attacks our knight in return, and eyes the a7-pawn.

We'll support the knight with e5, and prepare to develop our final minor piece.

2kr1b1r/ppp2pp1/2n2nq1/4p2p/3P4/2P1B1N1/.text: We can initiate a kingside attack with ...h5, aiming to go ...h4 and even ...h3!

2kr1b1r/ppp2ppp/4P1q1/8/3n2n1/2N1Q1N1/PP.text:
After ...Ng4, White's queen doesn't have much space to work with. 

We'll recapture the e6-pawn and also target the pawn on c2.

r3kb1r/ppp1pppp/2n2n2/3q4/3P4/2N5/PPP1NP.text:
White attacks our queen, which is what they do in 32% of the games.

Now we can shift our queen to the kingside.

r3kb1r/ppp1pppp/2n2n2/3q4/3P4/2P5/PP2NPP.text:
In 27% of the games, White supports the d4-pawn with c3.

We'll castle queenside, giving the option of a later ...e5 which puts further pressure on d4.

r3kb1r/ppp1pppp/2n2n2/7q/3P4/2N3N1/PPP2P.text:
White sees this and kicks out our queen.

We continue to locate our queen aggressively.

r3kb1r/ppp1pppp/2n2nq1/3P4/8/2N3N1/PPP2P.text:
White pushes d5 and attacks the c6-knight.

We don't have to move it!

r3kb1r/ppp1pppp/2n2nq1/8/3P4/2N1B1N1/PPP.text:
White could opt for the development with 9.Be3, which occurs in 31% of the games.

We can get the king into safety and exert pressure along the d-file.

rn1qkb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/3P4/3P2b1/8/PPP1BP.text:
Be2 occurs 40% of the time. White blocks the attack.

Retreating doesn't give Black any advantage, so we exchange.

rn1qkb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/3P4/3P4/8/PPP1NPPP.text:
This study is about 5.Nxe2, which happens in 74% of the games!

White wants to play c4, so we'll take back the pawn immediately, hitting g2.

rn2kb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/3q4/3P4/8/PPP1NPPP/.text:
White gets their king into safety.

We should continue developing.

rnbqkb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/3P4/3P4/8/PPP2PPP/.text:
In 16% of the games, White immediately pushes d4 and ignores their pawn on d5.

While the last chapter had more than 8 million games in its starting position, this one is down to 7 million games. It's still a considerable amount.

We'll develop our bishop and attack the white queen.

rnbqkbnr/ppp1pppp/8/3P4/8/8/PPPP1PPP/RNB.text:
White trades.

We develop our knight.

rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/RNB.text:
Welcome to the third chapter! 

Here, White pushes d4 on the third move instead of protecting the pawn on d5, and chooses to go 5.Nxe2. 

The second study of this chapter will analyze 5.Qxe2.  

Let's check it out!

2kr1b1r/ppp2ppp/2n1pn2/5q2/3P4/2N1BN2/PP.text: After castling queenside, we once again have ideas of attacking with ...g5, ...g4, this time supported with ...Rg8.

r3k2r/ppp1bppp/2n1pn2/5q2/2PP4/2N1BN2/PP.text:
White supports the d4-pawn.

We'll castle queenside.

r3k2r/ppp2ppp/2nbpn2/3q4/3P4/2P2N2/PP1NQ.text: White develops the knight to d2.

r3k2r/ppp2ppp/2nbpn2/7q/3P4/2P2N2/PP1NQP.text: The queen on h5 nicely supports the kingside attack, which will be initiated with ...g5 and ...g4.

r3kb1r/1pp2ppp/p3pn2/8/2P3q1/2N1B3/PP2QP.text: White's pawn sacrifice didn't offer anything and we have a comfortable position after ...Qg4.

r3kb1r/ppp2ppp/2n1pn2/3q4/2PP4/5N2/PP2QP.text:
In nearly half of the games, White attacks us with c4 here.

Retreating would be passive, but we can grab on d4 with a counter-attack.

r3kb1r/ppp2ppp/2n1pn2/3q4/3P4/2N2N2/PPP1.text:
White immediately develops and attacks our queen.

The queen goes to a typical square.

r3kb1r/ppp2ppp/2n1pn2/3q4/3P4/2P2N2/PP2Q.text:
White supports the d4-pawn with 8.c3.

Black now develops and prepares to castle.

r3kb1r/ppp2ppp/2n1pn2/5q2/3P4/2N1BN2/PPP.text: White develops and supports the d4-pawn.

r3kb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/3q4/2PN4/8/PP2QPPP/R.text:
White trades.

We'll recapture with the queen.

r3kb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/8/2P3q1/8/PP2QPPP/RN.text:
We'll move it to g4 and offer a queen trade. 

Black is better due to better-developed pieces and being a pawn up.

r3kb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/8/2Pq4/2N5/PP2QPPP/R.text:
White develops a minor piece instead of attacking our queen.

The threat is Nb5. Let's prevent it.

r3kb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/8/2Pq4/8/PP2QPPP/RNB.text: White attacks our queen on d4.

rn1qkb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/3P4/3P2b1/8/PPP1BP.text:
White attacks our bishop in return.

Retreating doesn't benefit us, so we exchange bishops.

rn1qkb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/3P4/3P4/8/PPP1QPPP.text:
This study covers 5.Qxe2, which is the second most popular move, occurring in 26% of the games.

c4 is the threat, so we'll regain the pawn by capturing on d5, also hitting the g2-pawn.

rn2k2r/ppp1bppp/4pn2/5q2/2PP4/2N2N2/PP2Q.text:
White castles.

Let's get the last minor piece out.

rn2kb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/3q4/3P4/5N2/PPP1QPP.text:
White covers it and prepares to castle.

Let's open up our dark-squared bishop.

rn2kb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/3q4/2PP4/5N2/PP2QPP.text:
In 30% of the games, White pushes c4 and attacks our queen with the pawn.

We don't have the possibility, seen elsewhere, of Nxd4, but we have an active square for the queen.

rn2kb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/3q4/3P4/5N2/PPP1QPP.text:
White castles.

Black continues to develop.

rn2kb1r/ppp2ppp/4pn2/5q2/2PP4/2N2N2/PP2Q.text:
White continues their development with Nc3.

Let's prepare kingside castling.

rnbqkb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/3P4/3P4/8/PPP2PPP/.text:
White controls some central squares with d4.

Developing with tempo is the way here!

rnbqkbnr/ppp1pppp/8/3P4/8/8/PPPP1PPP/RNB.text:
White captures.

We develop our knight.

rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/4P3/8/PPPP1PPP/RNB.text:
This study examines another option at the 5th move, which is Qxe2. 

Let's see it!

r2q1b1r/ppp2kpp/2n2n2/3P1b2/2P5/5P2/PP4P.text:
White tries to gain even more space in the center and attacks our knight.

Now the active pieces show their potential. We threaten a knight fork on c2.

r2q3r/ppp2kpp/5n2/2bP1b2/1nP5/N4P2/PP4PP.text:
White's king is in serious danger after ...Bc5.

...Re8+ is coming which will further exploit White's lack of development.

r2qk2r/ppp2ppp/4Pn2/2bP1b2/1nP5/N4P2/PP4.text:
The bishop pair is slicing through White's camp, making the king feel very unsafe.

The center will open up soon, which only benefits us.

r2qkb1r/ppp2Ppp/2n2n2/5b2/2PP4/5P2/PP4PP.text:
White continues to grab the pawns, this time with a check.

We don't mind our king being on f7. Black is far ahead in development as compensation.

r2qkb1r/ppp2ppp/2n1Pn2/3P1b2/2P5/5P2/PP4.text:
White connects the pawns and attacks our knight with d5.

The knight finds its active square on b4.

rn1qkb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/3P1b2/2PP4/5P2/PP4.text:
This move occurs in 50% of the games. 

White tries to hold on to the d5-pawn by pushing c4.

As we know from previous chapters, this structure is best challenged with ...e6.

rn1qkb1r/ppp1pppp/5n2/3P1b2/3P4/3B1P2/PP.text:
